title: Endorsement Rating Note — Additional Premium on a To-Value Increase of an Excess Flood Policy
content:
For an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** policy, the additional premium on a to-value increase of the excess dwelling limit is figured as set out in this note.

## Formal clause

The new excess dwelling limit of a to-value increase is the highest whole multiple of the tier's limit increment for which the building attachment point plus that limit stays within the tier's maximum percentage of the replacement cost value on the policy record, and never above the tier's maximum excess dwelling limit; the added limit is the new limit less the excess dwelling limit in force. The additional premium for an increase is the added limit divided by 1,000 times the layer rate per 1,000, multiplied by the charged share of the term, rounded to the cent once at the end. The layer rate per 1,000 is the latest term premium item booked for the current term (the term premium on the policy record where no term premium item is booked for that term) less the tier's loss-of-use charge, divided by the excess dwelling limit in thousands. The charged share of the term is the days from the day the increase takes effect to the term end, divided by the days from the term start to the term end, where the increase takes effect the tier's standard waiting period in calendar days after the signed request and full payment are received, and the share is nothing where that day falls on or after the term end.

A credit standing on the current term that covers the additional premium with its surplus lines tax and stamping fee counts as the full payment, received with the signed request.

The full-term premium as endorsed is the term premium before the increase plus the additional premium before the charged share of the term is applied, rounded to the cent.

Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read. The tier's limit increment, ceiling percentage, maximum excess dwelling limit, loss-of-use charge and waiting period are the tier's own figures; the replacement cost value, attachment point, limits and term dates are read from the policy record.

## Worked note (hypothetical figures, not a tier's)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Replacement cost value; building attachment point | 1200000; 250000 |
| Ceiling; limit increment; maximum excess dwelling limit | 100 percent; 50000; 1000000 |
| Excess dwelling limit in force | 700000 |
| Latest term premium item booked for the current term; loss-of-use charge | 1500.00; 100.00 |
| Term length; days left on the day the request and payment are received; waiting period | 365; 200; 30 |

Room under the ceiling is 950000, a whole multiple of 50000 and below 1000000, so the new limit is 950000 and the added limit 250000. The layer rate is 1400.00 divided by 700, that is 2.00 per 1,000, and the added limit's charge is 250 times 2.00, that is 500.00. The increase takes effect with 170 days left, so the charged share is 170 over 365 and the additional premium is 232.88. The full-term premium as endorsed is 1500.00 plus 500.00, that is 2000.00.
